It was developed to address limited processing capacity in hardware-accelerated volume rendering, where performance depends on fragment count, work per fragment, and cache utilization [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the technique was developed to address limited processing capacity in hardware-accelerated volume rendering, where performance depends on fragment count, work per fragment, and cache utilization. Source [S1] explicitly states in the passages: 'Roughly speaking, performance depends on the number of fragments processed in the fragment pipeline, the amount of work each fragment requires, and the utilization of the texture and framebuffer memory caches.' It also states the goal is to 'balance the available processing capacity' and 'improve interactivity in time-critical applications' by reducing fragment count (e.g., 'Drawing the context into a smaller viewport... is an effective way to reduce the number of fragments'). All specific factors mentioned in the claim are present in the evidence.
